comment: Paying $12.99 for Premium and still getting Spotify's own unskippable ads in my podcasts is the actual problem. Premium is supposed to mean no ads and it clearly doesn't for shows. I already moved my podcasts to Apple Podcasts and if they keep the ads on Premium I'm deleting my account.

Another bump. Apple Music is already cheaper and sounds better, and I keep flirting with it, but I'm stuck with Spotify because my shared family and friend playlists are years deep. Not leaving this time, just annoyed. Student price is still okay for me.

Lol, 'worth more' for a service that puts AI slop in my Discover Weekly and pays artists pennies. I already cancelled over the AI stuff and this just confirms they don't care about the people making the music. The price hike is pure profit.

Why do I have to pay more for features that should just come with the free app? I'm on free and I'm fine with that, but $12.99 for a handful of extras is ridiculous at this point. Sick of having to pay for basic stuff. Maybe I'll just use YouTube for full albums.

Another price hike and not one extra cent reaches the artists who make the music. Spotify takes its cut and the rights holders take theirs, and the artists get pennies after that. I already buy music directly when I can, and if payouts keep going to AI and stock music I'll go further in that direction.

Is anyone else seeing playlists play random songs instead of the ones I picked? Now the price is going up again. I'm keeping Spotify for my Liked Songs and downloads for now, but if the playlist thing doesn't get fixed I'll be checking Apple Music again.

Honestly the bump doesn't change much for me. I've been Premium for over ten years and I make most of my own playlists anyway. Discover Weekly still recycles the same top-40 songs, which is the annoying part, but the library is what I pay for. I can't see myself going back to Apple Music.
Price is whatever. I'm on 320 and Bluetooth compresses it anyway, so I don't see a reason to pay more for lossless. Still waiting on the hype to be real. Dolby on music is garbage too.

Duo going up $2, meh. I stick around for Discover Weekly and the new features once they finally show up on my account. The rollouts are slow and unpredictable though, the Your updates thing took forever. Well worth the wait when it lands, so I'm keeping it for now.

Paying more for an app that drops queues and restarts songs is wild, man. Lossless still sounds great on good speakers, but the Mix feature keeps closing and the perks vanished on my tablet. If the bugs aren't fixed soon I'm moving to Apple Music or YouTube Music, lol.

same issue here, tried reinstalling everything and the bug still comes back after every update. Now they want more money for Premium while this stays broken. I'll keep it since I'm hoping it gets fixed, but if not I'm going to YouTube Music. nothing worked for me so far.

I love the UI and my playlists are here, but the podcast side keeps getting worse. The New Episodes folder is gone and some episodes play in reverse, and now they're raising the price too. I'll stay for music in one app, but if the podcast stuff doesn't get sorted I'm going to Pocket Casts.

Honestly 12.99 is still worth it for me. It's cheaper than buying the albums I listen to, and ad-free listening plus downloads makes it a no-brainer. Yeah it's pricey and the podcast ads are annoying, but I'm not going anywhere.

Pricey-ish, but I'll take it. A family plan is still cheap per person and Spotify Connect across all my devices is worth every penny. The alternatives are only marginally better, so I'm not giving up the ecosystem over a bump like this.

The student price going from 5.99 to 6.99 is annoying but I'm still a student so I'll stay. My real worry is losing the Hulu bundle when the plan changes, especially since I already fight the re-verification every year. Full Premium at that price feels insane though.

Price up again and the algorithm still plays the same stuff. I already pay for YouTube Premium, which includes YouTube Music, so Spotify is getting harder to justify. I'm staying for Jam with my long distance friends for now, but the enshittification is real.

Great, another increase, and I'm still dealing with charges after cancelling. I buy multi-month blocks so I don't get hit monthly, but support keeps sending the same copy-paste reply. I'll keep my paid period and ask for fixes, but I'm not sure what I'm getting for the extra money.

Still the best deal going. Roughly $13 a month for nearly all the music ever made, plus offline downloads on my flights, is massively undervalued. Paying supports artists, which is why I don't mind the increase at all.

The price goes up again and I'm still paying the same as everyone else while lossless and AI playlists are region locked. The household plan is worth it for my parents, which is the only reason I haven't looked elsewhere. Discovery has gotten worse too, it's just frustrating.
Premium goes up again while shuffle is still broken, so I'm going back to free. Free actually shuffles better for my giant playlists anyway, which is insane. I'll deal with the ads.

Premium keeps going up and they keep removing or hiding stuff I actually use. Crossfade is still there, but the app is bloated, full of ads and absolute garbage. I'll keep paying for now because Spicetify fixes some of it, but I won't miss it if they keep going this way.

Price goes up and the free app is still ass, you can't pick songs without a paywall. I'd rather buy YouTube Premium than pay Spotify's price, and I'm still stuck listening to ads on free for now. Just pay for premium is easy to say when you're not the one paying.

Family plan price up again while the artist discography is still hidden. Desktop fullscreen only shows the album cover, what a joke. I'm still here for the catalog, but if they keep removing stuff I'm heading back to YouTube Music.

Raising prices while AI slop crowds out real artists in my Discover Weekly. I already left once and I'm not paying more for this. The artists barely get anything and Spotify doesn't check uploads. Maybe I'd come back if they actually crack down on fake music, but not at this price.

Family plan going to 21.99 hurts. It's still cheap per person, but the address verification and lockouts already make me want to dump it. No lossless at this price is brutal. It's still the practical choice for my household, so I'll stick with it for now.

The price bump is annoying but not enough to make me switch. Moving years of playlists to Apple Music would be a nightmare, and the search and multi-device sync are still the best for me. I'd rethink if they changed something I really hated.

Paying more for a service that still does not offer real lossless, while Tidal and others already have it at a lower price. Spotify isn't the bottleneck for me, but the bitrate is still low. I'll stick around for the recs and features, but lossless is still a gimmick until they fix it.

Prices keep going up while the app breaks after every update. Songs won't play the next track and support is useless. I'm keeping my playlists for now and hoping for a fix, but if this keeps up I'll cancel Premium and go to Amazon Music, which is cheaper anyway.
